core_obligations: Pull back the small-site restriction of G to the big fppf site, producing a quasi-coherent sheaf F and a canonical comparison map (proof lines 4073-4076).
Use the two hypotheses to show that the comparison map is an isomorphism on the small site of every flat locally finitely presented morphism (proof lines 4076-4079).
Conclude that the kernel and cokernel of the comparison map are parasitic for the fppf topology, so the comparison is an isomorphism on cohomology over such U (proof lines 4080-4092).
Finish by applying the known result for the quasi-coherent sheaf F (proof lines 4093-4095).
proof_roadmap: The comparison map and its source (proof lines 4073-4079).
Parasiticity of kernel and cokernel (proof lines 4080-4089).
Isomorphism on cohomology and the quasi-coherent case (proof lines 4089-4095).
difficulty_reason: For a sheaf of modules G on the big fppf site of a scheme S which is quasi-coherent on the small site and invariant under pullback along flat locally finitely presented morphisms, the lemma shows that the cohomology of G on a flat locally finitely presented U agrees with the cohomology of its small-site restriction (statement lines 4056-4070). The proof is a comparison of two short exact sequences: the author pulls back the small-site restriction to the big site to get a quasi-coherent F together with a comparison map which is an isomorphism on every small site of a flat locally finitely presented morphism, by the two hypotheses, and therefore has parasitic kernel and cokernel for the fppf topology (proof lines 4072-4089). The parasitic cohomology lemma makes the comparison map an isomorphism on cohomology, and the known result for the quasi-coherent F finishes (proof lines 4089-4095). The claim is H2: the notion of parasitic sheaves and the reduction to the quasi-coherent case are both cited, but the construction of the comparison map and the check that its kernel and cokernel are parasitic are written out in the span.
